WHAT AI ACTUALLY IS | It predicts the next word | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu | An AI assistant does not look up an answer. It reads your words and works out what should come next, one small piece at a time, thousands of times a second. | 1 | You type | Your request goes in as plain text. | 2 | It splits your text | Words become small pieces called tokens. | 3 | It predicts | It picks the most likely next piece, then the next, then the next. | 4 | You get an answer | Sentences appear that fit the shape of what you asked for. | What does this mean? | TOKEN  ? | MODEL  ?

WHAT AI ACTUALLY IS | It knows nothing about our company | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu | Everything it can say came from text it read before a fixed cut-off date. None of your company's files were in that text. | Public text it was trained on | Books, websites, manuals, forums — up to a fixed date. | What it can discuss confidently | General knowledge, language, structure, formatting. | What it knows about our company | Nothing at all, unless you type it in yourself. | This is why it can write a perfectly worded dispatch note and still invent the client's name. It is filling a gap in a sentence, not remembering a fact.

WHAT AI ACTUALLY IS | Three words you will hear daily | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu | Model | The trained system that produces the answer. ChatGPT, Copilot and Gemini are apps built around a model. | Prompt | Everything you type in. Your request, plus any facts you decide to give it. | Output | What comes back. Always a draft you are responsible for. Never a source you can quote. | What does this mean? | PROMPT  ? | OUTPUT  ?

SEARCH OR ASSISTANT? | Search finds pages. AI writes text. | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu | SEARCH ENGINE | Google, Bing, the company intranet | Returns links to pages that other people wrote | Right choice when you need a source you can quote | Everyone who searches the same words sees the same list | Will not rewrite your email or shorten your report | AI ASSISTANT | Copilot, ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude | Returns new text written for your exact request | Right choice when you need a draft, summary or rewrite | Gives a slightly different answer every time you ask | Cannot promise that any fact inside it is correct

SEARCH OR ASSISTANT? | Which one do I open? | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu | Do I need a page someone else wrote, or new text of my own? | A PAGE | Open search | A GST circular, a supplier's spec sheet, a government notification, a news report. You need the actual page, because you will have to show it to someone. | NEW TEXT | Open the AI assistant | A reply to an unhappy client, a summary of a 12-page site report, a first draft of an SOP. You already have the facts and only need the wording.

YOUR FIRST TWO MINUTES | Do this now: your first 90 seconds | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu | 1 | Open your approved AI assistant. On most company laptops this is Microsoft Copilot, in Edge or inside Teams. | 2 | Click into the message box at the bottom of the screen. | 3 | Select the whole prompt on the right, copy it, paste it in, and press Enter. | 4 | Read what comes back. Notice that it used every fact you gave it, and invented nothing. | Select + copy | Copy this prompt | Write a short, polite email to a customer whose delivery is late. Facts: order 4471, promised 12 March, now expected 15 March, delayed by a transport strike. Tone: apologetic but calm. Under 120 words. End with "Regards, Dispatch Team". | This works exactly as written. Swap in your own order number and dates afterwards.

YOUR FIRST TWO MINUTES | The same job, asked two ways | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu | VAGUE REQUEST | You type:  write email about late delivery | You get back a six-paragraph letter with no order number, no dates, and an apology for "any inconvenience caused". | You now spend ten minutes repairing it. You could have written it yourself in eight. | SPECIFIC REQUEST | You type the prompt from the last slide: order number, both dates, the reason, the tone, the word limit. | You get back a 110-word email with the correct dates, one clear apology and a firm new delivery date. | You spend 60 seconds checking the dates against the tracking sheet, then send it. | The difference was not the AI tool. It was the four facts you took ten seconds to type.

YOUR FIRST TWO MINUTES | Turn rough notes into a report | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu | This is the most useful thing most people do with AI all week. You already made the notes. You just need them in sentences. | Select + copy | Copy this prompt | Turn these site-visit notes into a 180-word report for my manager. Keep every fact. Do not add anything I have not written. Notes: visited Chakan plant 4 March; two of six machines idle; operator says spare part on order since 20 Feb; production down about 30 percent; supervisor asking for a follow-up visit next week. | Paste it as-is to see the shape, then replace the notes with your own. | WHAT COMES BACK | A 180-word report with a one-line summary at the top, the five facts in order, and a closing line about the follow-up visit. | Every number in it — six machines, 20 February, 30 per cent — came from your notes, because you told it to add nothing. | Your job now is 60 seconds of checking, not 30 minutes of writing.

YOUR FIRST TWO MINUTES | When it is 80% right, correct it | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu | Select + copy | Copy this correction prompt | Keep the structure and the tone exactly as they are. Change three things: the delivery date is 15 March, not 12 March; delete the final paragraph; make the apology one sentence instead of two. | Say what to keep, then say what to change. In that order. | WHY THIS WORKS | Starting again gives you a different answer with the same gaps, because the gaps came from your first prompt. | Naming what to keep stops it rewriting the good 80%. | Three specific changes work far better than "make it better", which it cannot act on.

WHERE IT HELPS, WHERE IT BREAKS | Three things it is good at | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu | Turning facts into text | Emails, summaries, SOP drafts, meeting notes. You supply the facts, it supplies the sentences. | Reshaping what you give it | A long report into five bullets. A Hindi note into English. A messy list into a clean table. | Getting you unstuck | Ten subject lines to choose from. Questions to ask a supplier. A structure for a proposal you are staring at blankly.

WHERE IT HELPS, WHERE IT BREAKS | Where it breaks | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu | It can be completely wrong and still sound completely sure. | There is no warning sign, no change of tone, no "I think". Every answer arrives with the same confidence. | Numbers you did not give it — prices, GST rates, stock levels, distances, penalties | Anything after its cut-off date — this month's circular, yesterday's rate change | Our own facts — client names, internal policies, system names, who approves what | Legal, tax or medical points you would act on without a human checking them | What does this mean? | HALLUCINATION  ?

WHERE IT HELPS, WHERE IT BREAKS | Should I use AI for this task? | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu | Do I already know the facts, and can I check the answer? | NO | Get the facts first | If you cannot check the answer, you cannot use it. Take the real number from the system, the circular or your manager, and then come back to the assistant. | YES | Go ahead | You give the facts, it gives the wording, you check it before it leaves your desk. This covers most of the writing in an ordinary office week.

USING IT SAFELY | Four habits that keep you safe | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu | Give it facts, never files. Type the order number and the dates. Do not paste the contract. | Check every number, name and date yourself before the text goes anywhere. | Treat the output as your draft that you edited. Never present it as a source. | Use the tool the company has approved: [COMPANY INPUT NEEDED: name of the approved AI assistant]. A personal login puts our text on someone else's account.

USING IT SAFELY | Four checks before you press send | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu | Every date and number matches a system or document you actually opened. | Every name is spelled the way the customer spells it, not the way it sounds. | Nothing has been added that you did not supply — read once looking only for that. | You would be comfortable if the customer could see the prompt you typed.

USING IT SAFELY | Five mistakes people really make | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu | 1 | Pasting a full customer contract in "just to summarise it" | Client data leaves the company. Reportable under India's DPDP Act and UAE data protection law. | 2 | Asking for a live figure — today's GST rate, current stock | It answers from memory. A confidently wrong number lands in the monthly MIS. | 3 | Sending the first draft without reading it | Invented dates and order numbers reach the client with your name at the bottom. | 4 | Typing four words, getting a vague answer, giving up | You decide "AI is useless". The prompt was the problem, not the tool. | 5 | Using a personal ChatGPT login for company work | No record, no control, and no way to delete the data if we are ever asked to.

CHOOSE WHAT YOU'D DO | Monday, 9:40 am | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu | A client in Sharjah emails: "Your team promised delivery on the 12th. Nothing has arrived. Explain." You have the tracking sheet open. Your manager is in a meeting until 11. | OPTION A | Paste the client's email and the full tracking sheet into ChatGPT and ask it to write the reply for you. | See what happens | OPTION B | Type only the three facts you already know into the approved assistant and ask for a 100-word reply. | See what happens | OPTION C | Wait for your manager to come out of the meeting before replying to the client. | See what happens

You just sent client data outside the company | The tracking sheet carries the client's name, address and order values — plus every other customer on the page. Once it sits in a personal AI account, the company cannot retrieve it, delete it, or tell an auditor where it went. | THE RULE | Facts, not files. Type the two dates and the reason. The document stays where it is. | Back to the situation  → | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu

Correct — this is exactly the right use | You gave it the order number, the promised date and the reason. A calm 100-word reply came back in 20 seconds. You checked both dates against the tracking sheet, added the new delivery date, and sent it at 9:44. | THE RULE | You supply the facts and the final check. The assistant supplies the sentences in between. | Back to the situation  → | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu

Safe — but the client waits two hours | Nothing goes wrong, and nothing goes right. The client sends a sharper email at 11:15. Your manager now has an escalation to handle instead of a delay — and you had every fact you needed at 9:40. | THE RULE | Use AI for the drafting. Use your manager for the decisions — not for the typing. | Back to the situation  → | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu

QUIZ  ·  QUESTION 1 OF 5 | What should you assume? | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu | You asked an AI assistant for a courier's customer care number. It replied with a ten-digit number, straight away. | A | It looked it up on the website just now | B | It is probably right, because it sounded certain | C | It may be invented — check it on the official site before using it | D | AI tools are not able to produce phone numbers

Not quite — here's what actually happens | YOU CHOSE  A.  It looked it up on the website just now | It did not open any website. Unless the tool visibly shows you a link it visited, it produced that number the same way it produces a sentence — by predicting what a courier helpline number usually looks like. Digits are exactly the kind of detail this goes wrong on. | REMEMBER | Sounding sure and being right are two different things. | Try this question again  → | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu

Not quite — here's what actually happens | YOU CHOSE  B.  It is probably right, because it sounded certain | Certainty is not evidence. The tool writes every answer in the same confident tone, whether it is repeating something it saw a million times or filling a gap. There is no built-in "I am unsure" signal for you to look for. | REMEMBER | Sounding sure and being right are two different things. | Try this question again  → | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu

Correct — here's why | YOU CHOSE  C.  It may be invented — check it on the official site before using it | Correct. Treat any number, name or date in an AI answer as unverified until you have seen it at the source. Ten seconds on the official website stops a wrong number going into a client email under your name. | REMEMBER | Sounding sure and being right are two different things. | Next question  → | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu

Not quite — here's what actually happens | YOU CHOSE  D.  AI tools are not able to produce phone numbers | They will produce one happily, and that is the problem. It will have the right number of digits, the right format and the right area code, and still be wrong. Nothing about it will look suspicious. | REMEMBER | Sounding sure and being right are two different things. | Try this question again  → | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu

QUIZ  ·  QUESTION 2 OF 5 | Which task fits AI best? | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu | You have four jobs on your desk this morning. Only one of them plays to what an AI assistant is actually good at. | A | "Tell me our current stock of 40mm bearings" | B | "Turn these six bullet points from my site visit into a 200-word report" | C | "Decide whether we should terminate this supplier" | D | "Tell me what the new circular from Head Office says"

Not quite — here's what actually happens | YOU CHOSE  A.  "Tell me our current stock of 40mm bearings" | It has no connection to your stock system and never will unless someone builds one. It will either refuse, or produce a number that looks completely plausible and is completely made up. Get this from the system. | REMEMBER | You bring the facts. It brings the sentences. | Try this question again  → | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu

Correct — here's why | YOU CHOSE  B.  "Turn these six bullet points from my site visit into a 200-word repor | This is the sweet spot. You already hold every fact. The tool only has to do the wording, and you can check each line against your own bullets in under a minute. | REMEMBER | You bring the facts. It brings the sentences. | Next question  → | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu

Not quite — here's what actually happens | YOU CHOSE  C.  "Decide whether we should terminate this supplier" | This is a judgement with money, contracts and relationships attached. The tool has none of the history, none of the contract, and carries none of the consequences. Ask it to list the questions worth considering — never to make the call. | REMEMBER | You bring the facts. It brings the sentences. | Try this question again  → | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu

Not quite — here's what actually happens | YOU CHOSE  D.  "Tell me what the new circular from Head Office says" | It has never seen that circular, so anything it says about it is invented. If the circular is not confidential you can paste the text in and ask for a summary — that turns it into a task it can actually do. | REMEMBER | You bring the facts. It brings the sentences. | Try this question again  → | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu

QUIZ  ·  QUESTION 3 OF 5 | Which of these is safe to type in? | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu | You are about to paste something into an approved AI assistant to help you draft a reply. | A | The customer's signed contract, so it can summarise it | B | A colleague's salary, to check whether a raise is fair | C | The two dates and the reason for a delay, with no names | D | Nothing at all — AI is too risky to use

Not quite — here's what actually happens | YOU CHOSE  A.  The customer's signed contract, so it can summarise it | That contract holds names, prices and terms the customer trusted us with. Pasting it copies all of that onto a system the company does not control and cannot audit. This is the most common serious mistake people make. | REMEMBER | Give it enough to write with. Never enough to identify anyone. | Try this question again  → | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu

Not quite — here's what actually happens | YOU CHOSE  B.  A colleague's salary, to check whether a raise is fair | Salary is personal data about a named person. Moving it outside the systems approved for HR data is a privacy breach by itself, whatever the AI answers. The answer is not the problem — the paste is. | REMEMBER | Give it enough to write with. Never enough to identify anyone. | Try this question again  → | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu

Correct — here's why | YOU CHOSE  C.  The two dates and the reason for a delay, with no names | Facts without identifiers. The tool has everything it needs to write the email and nothing that could harm anyone if it leaked. Make this your default habit and you will rarely have to think about it again. | REMEMBER | Give it enough to write with. Never enough to identify anyone. | Next question  → | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu

Not quite — here's what actually happens | YOU CHOSE  D.  Nothing at all — AI is too risky to use | This is a mistake in the other direction. Refusing to use an approved tool costs you hours every week and leaves you behind colleagues who use it well. The skill is knowing what to leave out, not avoiding the tool. | REMEMBER | Give it enough to write with. Never enough to identify anyone. | Try this question again  → | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu

QUIZ  ·  QUESTION 4 OF 5 | The answer is 80% right. Now what? | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu | The structure and tone are exactly what you wanted, but one date is wrong and the last paragraph is not needed. | A | Rewrite the whole thing yourself | B | Send it — 80% is good enough for an internal note | C | Tell it what is wrong and ask for a corrected version | D | Send the same prompt again and hope for a better answer

Not quite — here's what actually happens | YOU CHOSE  A.  Rewrite the whole thing yourself | You just threw away 80% of finished work. Tell it what is wrong instead: "Keep the structure, but the date is 15 March not 12 March, and remove the last paragraph." That takes ten seconds. | REMEMBER | Correct it. Do not restart it. | Try this question again  → | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu

Not quite — here's what actually happens | YOU CHOSE  B.  Send it — 80% is good enough for an internal note | The missing 20% is exactly where the wrong dates live. Internal notes get forwarded. Wrong facts travel further than you expect, and your name stays attached to them the whole way. | REMEMBER | Correct it. Do not restart it. | Try this question again  → | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu

Correct — here's why | YOU CHOSE  C.  Tell it what is wrong and ask for a corrected version | This is the whole skill. The second attempt is almost always the good one. Be specific about what to keep as well as what to change, or it will rewrite the parts that were already fine. | REMEMBER | Correct it. Do not restart it. | Next question  → | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu

Not quite — here's what actually happens | YOU CHOSE  D.  Send the same prompt again and hope for a better answer | You will get a different answer with the same gaps, because the gaps came from the prompt. Repeating an unchanged prompt is the most common way people waste time with these tools. | REMEMBER | Correct it. Do not restart it. | Try this question again  → | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu

QUIZ  ·  QUESTION 5 OF 5 | Where did that figure come from? | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu | Your manager points at a number in your monthly report and asks where it came from. It came from an AI answer. | A | Tell her the AI assistant provided it | B | Find the figure in the real system or document and quote that | C | Say you calculated it yourself | D | Remove the figure from the report

Not quite — here's what actually happens | YOU CHOSE  A.  Tell her the AI assistant provided it | "The AI said so" is not a source. Your manager cannot act on it, cannot defend it to a client, and if the figure is wrong the report is still yours. Find the real source before the report goes out. | REMEMBER | AI output is a draft. It is never a source. | Try this question again  → | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu

Correct — here's why | YOU CHOSE  B.  Find the figure in the real system or document and quote that | Right. Every number in anything you sign should be traceable to a system, a document or a named person. AI can help you write the sentence around the number. It cannot be the reason the number is there. | REMEMBER | AI output is a draft. It is never a source. | See the recap  → | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu

Not quite — here's what actually happens | YOU CHOSE  C.  Say you calculated it yourself | This turns a checkable mistake into a false statement. If the figure is later found to be wrong, the problem is no longer the figure — it is that you said something untrue about where it came from. | REMEMBER | AI output is a draft. It is never a source. | Try this question again  → | AI-01  ·  AI Fundamentals | Inducto Learning Library | Menu

Not quite — here's what actually happens | YOU CHOSE  D.  Remove the figure from the report | Better than inventing a source, but you have thrown away information the report needed.
